<h>Invitatorium</h>
<r>Ant.</r> Dóminum, Deum nostrum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>Ant.</r> Dóminum, Deum nostrum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>V</c>eníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
<r>Ant.</r> Dóminum, Deum nostrum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
<r>Ant.</r> Dóminum, Deum nostrum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>H</c>ódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
<r>Ant.</r> Dóminum, Deum nostrum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.

<h>Invitatory</h>
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord is our God * Come, let us adore Him.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord is our God * Come, let us adore Him.
<c>C</c>ome let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord is our God * Come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>or the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.
<r>Ant.</r> Come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>or the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. <n>(genuflect)</n> Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord is our God * Come, let us adore Him.
<c>T</c>oday if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.
<r>Ant.</r> Come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>orty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord is our God * Come, let us adore Him.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

b.1831ece28b:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>D</c>écimo octávo Kaléndas Decémbris Luna quarta. Anno Dómini 2026
<h>S</h>ancti Iósaphat, e sancti Basilíi Ordine, Epíscopi Polocénsis et Mártyris, cuius dies natális recensétur prídie Idus Novémbris.
<h>G</h>angris, in Paphlagónia, sancti Hypátii Epíscopi, qui, a magna Nicǽna Sýnodo rédiens, a Novatiánis hæréticis in via lapídibus impetítus, Martyr occúbuit.
<h>H</h>eracléæ, in Thrácia, natális sanctórum Mártyrum Clementíni, Theódoti et Philómeni.
<h>A</h>lexandríæ sancti Serapiónis Mártyris, quem persecutóres, sub Décio Príncipe, ita crudelíssimis affecérunt supplíciis, ut cunctas ei iunctúras membrórum prius sólverent, eúmque póstea de superióribus domus suæ præcipitárent; atque ille sic gloriósus Christi Martyr efficerétur.
<h>T</h>recis, in Gállia, sancti Venerándi Mártyris, sub Aureliáno Imperatóre.
<h>I</h>n Gállia sanctæ Venerándæ Vírginis, quæ, sub Antoníno Imperatóre et Asclepíade Prǽside, martýrii corónam accépit.
<h>E</h>méssæ, in Phœnícia, pássio plurimárum sanctárum mulíerum, quæ, sub sævíssimo Arabum duce Mady, ob Christi fidem, crudelíssime tortæ atque necátæ sunt.
<h>B</h>onóniæ sancti Iucúndi, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
<h>A</h>ugæ, in Gállia, tránsitus sancti Lauréntii, Epíscopi Dublinénsis.
<h>A</h>lgáriæ, in Africa, beáti Serapiónis, qui, primus ex Ordine beátæ Maríæ de Mercéde redemptiónis captivórum, pro captívis fidélibus rediméndis et Christiánæ fídei prædicatióne actus in crucem et membrátim disséctus, martýrii palmam méruit obtinére.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.406a5d5614:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>N</c>ovember 14th 2026, the 4th day of the Moon,
<h>O</h>n the morrow we keep in England the feast of holy Erconwald, Bishop of London, who was famous for many miracles, and of whom mention is made upon the last day of April.
<h>O</h>n the morrow we keep the feast of the holy martyr Josaphat, of the Order of St. Basil, Archbishop of Polotsk, of whom mention is made upon the 12th day of this present month of November.
<h>U</h>pon the same 14th day of November, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Gangra, in Paphlagonia, the holy martyr Hypatius, Bishop (of that see,) who was stoned to death by the Novatian heretics on his way back from the great Council of Nicea.
<h>A</h>t Heraclea, in Thrace, the holy martyrs Clementine, Theodotus, and Philomenus.
<h>A</h>t Alexandria, the holy martyr Serapion, whom the persecutors under the Emperor Decius most cruelly tormented until they dislocated all his joints, and then cast him down headlong from the top of his own house, and so made him a martyr for Christ.
<h>A</h>t Troyes, in Gaul, under the Emperor Aurelian, the holy martyr Venerandus.
<h>L</h>ikewise in Gaul, the holy Virgin Veneranda, who received the crown of martyrdom under the Emperor Antonine and Asclepiades the President.
<h>A</h>t Emesa, many holy Women, who, for Christ's faith's sake, were most cruelly tortured and murdered under the savage Arab chief Mady.
<h>A</h>t Bologna, the holy Confessor Jucundus, Bishop (of that see.)
<h>A</h>t Eu, in Gaul, (in the year 1181,) the passing of holy Lorcan Ua Tuathail, Archbishop of Dublin.
<h>A</h>t Algiers, in Africa, (in the year 1240,) the blessed Serapion, the first martyr of the Order of Blessed Mary of Ransom for the Redemption of the Captive Faithful and the Preaching of the Christian Faith. He won his crown by being fastened to a cross and cut limb from limb.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
